name: Tortillitas de Camarones
desc: Lacy, crisp fritters of chickpea and wheat flour with tiny whole shrimp in them, a Cádiz speciality. You eat the shrimp eyes and all, and after the third one you stop minding. Restores 160 HP.

name: Churros con Chocolate
desc: Ridged sticks of fried dough with a cup of hot chocolate thick enough to stand them up in. A Spanish breakfast, or the end of a very long night. Restores 120 HP.

name: Pescaíto Frito
desc: A paper cone of little fried fish, squid rings and anchovies, dusted in flour and fried in olive oil: Andalusia's answer to fish and chips. Squeeze the lemon over it. Restores 220 HP.

name: Loukoumades
desc: Little balls of fried dough soaked in honey syrup, sold hot in a paper tray. Turkish Cypriots make the same thing and call them lokma, and both sides queue for them at fairs. Restores 140 HP.

name: Koupepia
desc: Vine leaves rolled round minced meat and rice, Cypriot style, simmered with lemon. Every family on the island makes them, and every family is sure theirs are right. Restores 200 HP.

name: Şeftali Kebab
desc: Little sausages of minced meat, onion and parsley wrapped in caul fat and grilled over charcoal, eaten in pitta with salad. Turkish Cypriots call it şeftali kebabı and Greek Cypriots sheftalia: lamb on one side, usually pork on the other, the same smoke over both. Restores 230 HP.

name: Ayran
desc: Cold yoghurt whisked with water and a pinch of salt, drunk with grilled meat all over the north. Very good at putting out a chilli. Restores 90 HP.
